summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the node around AI-era identity, data security, exposure management, and control layers. The reference anchor is Palo Alto Networks after closing CyberArk and launching AI-era identity capabilities. The underfollowed lane favors mid-cap software/security names whose products are not always labeled as AI infrastructure but may become more necessary as enterprises deploy AI agents, expose sensitive data to copilots, and automate hybrid-cloud workflows. This pass intentionally avoids GPU/cloud megacaps and focuses on control-plane software exposure. Expanded the node with a two-lane universe focused on second-order AI control-layer beneficiaries rather than accelerator or hyperscaler leaders. The strongest underfollowed candidates in this pass are PDF Solutions for secure semiconductor-manufacturing connectivity/orchestration, Tenable for AI/cloud/identity exposure management, and PagerDuty for AIOps, incident response, and automation workflow control. CyberArk is included as a higher-attention reference anchor because machine identity and AI-agent identity are likely core control-layer chokepoints, but its market cap and visibility make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane. Layer 1B expands the universe around the hypothesis that enterprise AI deployment shifts bottlenecks toward identity governance, machine/AI-agent permissions, data security posture, observability, and automated incident control.
